title: Averaging a lopsided die
hook: Five faces show 1, one shows 6. What do averages of many rolls look like?

knows: how to average a list of numbers
that averages of many rolls settle near the die's mean
doesNotKnow: that the averages also take on a bell shape, whatever one roll looks like
why bell curves are so common

misconception: An average of many rolls of a lopsided die is lopsided like a single roll.
objective: The learner can describe how the histogram of averages changes from two spikes (1 roll) to one hump around 1.83 (30 rolls), and say that averaging many random pieces tends towards a bell shape.
keyState: Group size raised from 1 (two spikes: 1,648 ones, 352 sixes) through 2, 5, 10 to 30 (one hump around 1.83; the averages averaged 1.85).

claims.text: A die with five faces showing 1 and one showing 6 averages 11/6 = 1.83 per roll.
claims.source: (5 x 1 + 6)/6 = 11/6 = 1.833 (MEAN in src/demos/probability/averages-turn-bell-shaped/model.ts). Single-roll SD = 5 x sqrt(1/6 x 5/6) = 1.863.

claims.text: On the stage, 2,000 single rolls gave 1,648 ones and 352 sixes; 2,000 averages of 30 rolls formed one hump around 1.83 and averaged 1.85.
claims.source: run(n) in model.ts, mulberry32 seed 1833 + n, untuned (the first seed tried). Means of the averages for n = 1, 2, 5, 10, 30: 1.880, 1.775, 1.868, 1.824, 1.845. Over seeds 1-500 at n = 30 the mean of the averages had middle 95% 1.819-1.850 (median 1.834).

claims.text: At 30 rolls the hump is only slightly lopsided.
claims.source: Sample skewness of the 2,000 averages (skew() in model.ts): 1.70 (n = 1), 1.36, 0.79, 0.59, 0.31 (n = 30); theory 1.79/sqrt(n) = 0.33 at n = 30. 97.9% of the n = 30 averages lie within 2 standard errors (2 x 1.863/sqrt(30) = 0.68) of 1.83.

claims.text: Many small random pieces added up tend to a bell: the central limit theorem.
claims.source: Central limit theorem for i.i.d. variables with finite variance (Feller, An Introduction to Probability Theory and Its Applications, vol. 2, ch. VIII). Stated loosely: no conditions beyond finite variance are claimed.

recall.question: Single waiting times at a counter are very lopsided: most short, a few very long. What shape is the chart of daily average waits (each day averaging 200 customers)?
options: Roughly a bell around the typical average
recall.why: Averaging many independent pieces smooths any shape toward a bell centred on the mean; the lopsidedness shrinks as the group grows.
